🌎 BEYOND THE 956

British actor and comedian Russell Brand was convicted Thursday of rape and sexual assault in a London court, and was taken into custody ahead of his sentencing.

A jury at Southwark Crown Court found Brand, 51, guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. The jury cleared him of two other rape charges and one count of attempted indecent assault.

The charges involved six women and dated back to incidents between 1999 and 2009. Brand had denied all of the charges and pleaded not guilty.

Judge Joel Bennathan denied Brand's request for bail and remanded him into custody, warning that he faces a significant prison sentence when he returns to court for sentencing on Monday, November 9.

London Metropolitan Police Detective Superintendent Andy Furphy praised the women who came forward, calling the conviction a testament to their extraordinary courage, resilience, and determination.

The women in the case are entitled to lifelong anonymity under UK law, and their names have not been published.

Update — November 9, 2026

On Monday, November 9, Judge Joel Bennathan sentenced Brand, 51, to 10 years and six months in prison at Southwark Crown Court in London, following his November 5 conviction on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. Brand will serve two-thirds of the sentence in custody before being released on licence, the court said.

Before sentencing, four of the women in the case gave victim impact statements to the court. The judge praised the determination and bravery of the women who came forward, and said Brand had acted as though fame put him above the rules ordinary people live by.

Metropolitan Police Detective Superintendent Andy Furphy said Brand "has been held accountable for his crimes" and that he hoped the outcome provides the victims some measure of closure. The Metropolitan Police said it is still investigating two further rape allegations against Brand. Brand has denied all charges and pleaded not guilty; no appeal had been reported as of publication.

Sources: WorldStar (@worldstar) on Instagram; Metropolitan Police; Reuters; USA Today. Update sources: USA Today, Nov. 9, 2026; Associated Press via WHRO, Nov. 9, 2026; Metropolitan Police statement, Nov. 9, 2026.

title: Beyond the 956: Russell Brand convicted of rape and sexual assault, taken into custody
